identification: Box of three unframed prints: (1) Vanity Fair 'Men of the Day No. 1071' colour chromolithograph 'Jimmy' (golfer James Braid) by Spy (Sir Leslie Ward), published 26 June 1907, loose; (2) a Punch-style hand-coloured black-and-white cartoon 'Quick Bridge' ('One Club, One Diamond, One Heart, One Moment') on a white mount, probably 1920s-30s Punch; (3) a second Vanity Fair print of a bearded academic in cap and gown holding a birch broom, in a mount in plastic wrap, caption not legible (1870s-80s style Ape/Spy). Cannot tell from photos whether the Vanity Fair prints are originals or later reproductions.

Print 3: 'Vanity Fair' header, Spy/Ape-style signature at lower right, caption illegible through plastic.

If the Braid print is an original, a golf print can retail A$150-300 at dealers, but I found no dated sold price at that level.
